entries.title: The Guide can offer Referee to reviewers
entries.body: When you tell the Guide chat that you are refereeing a piece, or assessing it for a journal, conference or funder, it is set up to offer Referee, the mode that helps a peer reviewer, as a button, even with Experimental features switched off. Nothing opens until you press it. It is also asked to mention that the article's text went to an AI service when you added it. In ordinary Chat and the command bar, Referee stays behind the switch.

entries.title: Live conversation uses a different AI by default
entries.body: Talking to the article out loud uses a different AI service by default. With Experimental features switched on, a small arrow on the Live button lets you choose between it and the earlier one, Realtime; if you had already chosen Realtime, that choice is kept. The privacy page names the services involved.

entries.title: Metadata page uses the mode bar's names
entries.body: The Metadata page's list of what the AI did to an article, and its rows for running a step again, use the mode bar's names, such as Summary › Thread, with a line under each saying what it is. Typing "rerun brief" or "rerun fuller" in the command bar rebuilds both the Brief and Fuller summaries together.

entries.title: Guide replies no longer trail a stray sentence
entries.body: A Guide reply that offered to save something you had already saved could add a second, stray sentence onto the end of its answer. The Guide now ends its turn once the answer and its next-step buttons are written, which stopped this in our tests.
